sentences.text: The genus Ceratocaudia contains only one species, C. antiqua, known from a partial skeleton.
Its name comes from Greek and Latin words meaning 'horn' and 'tail', referring to a horn-like crest on the front tail vertebrae.
Histological analysis and non-traumatic pathology suggest the holotype was an old, senescent individual.
The holotype was collected from the Khadir Uplift of the Kaladongar Formation in the Kutch district of Gujarat, India.
These fossils are now housed at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay in Mumbai, India, under accession numbers IITBR3–IITBR59.
Reconstructed muscle models suggest the tail of Ceratocaudia may have been used to deter predators.
The coexistence of a large sauropod suggests niche partitioning with Ceratocaudia, though their specific ecological roles remain unknown due to the lack of cranial material.
Ceratocaudia belongs to the class Saurischia.
It is classified as a macronarian sauropod.
Phylogenetic analyses place Ceratocaudia within Macronaria but outside Titanosauriformes, suggesting it is one of the oldest macronarians and indicating a global pre-Bajocian distribution.
Ceratocaudia lived during the Jurassic period, specifically from the Pliensbachian to the Bajocian stages.
The time range for Ceratocaudia is estimated to be from the Hettangian to the Bajocian, between 201.4 and 168.2 million years ago.
It lived in an environment containing abundant petrified wood and brackish-water bivalves such as Protocardia and Indocorbula.
